strengths: Addresses a well-motivated, practically relevant problem in LLM alignment: the diversity-quality tradeoff
Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation across 13 metrics (11 diversity × 2 quality), multiple datasets, model families, and both automatic and human evaluation

Thoughtful evaluation design: separates lexical vs. semantic diversity, extends to discourse-level diversity for long-form generation, uses Coverage/Dominance metrics from multi-objective optimization
Practical, deployable approach requiring only inference-time modifications with no retraining
Consistent empirical results across datasets with 21.3% best-case joint improvement
Strong experimental methodology including ablation studies (random routing, aligned-aligned collaboration, -JUDGE) and contribution analysis
Well-presented with clear motivation, effective visualizations, and honest discussion of failure modes and limitations
Extensive supplementary materials with implementation details and annotation protocols support reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: model combination and weighted routing are well-established; relies heavily on Fei et al. (2025)'s superficial alignment hypothesis; routing strategies are simple heuristics

Unresolved critical failure mode: Section 6.2 identifies inherent early stopping when routing to base model that can truncate outputs; proposed 'restart sampling' solution is unsatisfying and adds complexity

Router design lacks principled foundation: multiple ad-hoc strategies without systematic design methodology; no clear guidance for selecting routers on new domains; hyperparameter γ requires tuning with unclear selection methodology
Methodological concern: human evaluation uses 'matched quality' comparison which may artificially favor BACO and mask scenarios where it struggles
Shallow theoretical understanding: why these specific heuristics work is not explained beyond superficial alignment hypothesis
Incomplete comparisons: missing recent diversity-promotion methods (2024-2025); NUDGING comparison limited to quality; ensemble baselines are relatively weak
Evaluation scale limitations: only 10 samples per prompt; moderate inter-rater agreement on diversity (κ=0.166-0.244); human evaluation on only 20 prompts per dataset
Computational cost not substantiated: runtime overhead of dual-model inference not reported; efficiency claims based on superficial alignment not empirically validated
Limited scope and generalization: only 2 model families tested; requires availability of both base and aligned versions; unclear performance with significant model divergence
Missing key analyses: frequency/severity of early stopping, statistical significance testing, sensitivity to alignment quality, detailed failure mode investigation

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing recognized diversity degradation in aligned LLMs
Comprehensive evaluation scope including three diverse datasets, 13 metrics, and discourse-level analysis for long-form generation
Practical inference-time approach requiring no fine-tuning or specialized prompting
Controllability via adjustable threshold parameter enabling diverse-quality spectrum navigation
Honest identification and reporting of failure modes (early stopping problem in Section 6.2)
Human evaluation complementing automatic metrics on quality, diversity, and creativity
weaknesses: Critical unresolved failure mode: inherent early stopping when routing toward base models directly contradicts single-pass inference claim; proposed solution (restart sampling) is inadequate and unevaluated
Limited novelty: incremental over Fei et al. (2025) NUDGING with simple heuristic routing strategies (-P, -H, -FC, -PUNC) lacking principled design methodology

Evaluation methodology concerns: 100+ comparisons across 22+ spaces without statistical significance testing or multiple testing correction; results often marginal (Table 3: -RAND at 0.451 vs -P-PUNC at 0.474 coverage)
Ad-hoc router selection: no principled way to choose routing strategies for new tasks; appears to involve trying many combinations and reporting best performers
Effectiveness depends critically on having diverse base model: AACO (aligned-aligned) achieves only 0.014 coverage vs BACO's 0.474, limiting applicability and reintroducing alignment safety risks
Random routing nearly as effective as designed routing: -RAND achieves 21.7% dominance vs -P-PUNC's 31.0%, undermining the value of careful router design
Weak baselines: compared primarily to temperature-adjusted single models and ensemble methods; missing comparisons to other inference-time diversity methods and baselines at different temperatures
Small human evaluation: only 20 prompts per dataset with 4 annotators; moderate inter-rater agreement (κ=0.166-0.268) suggests inherent subjectivity
Presentation masks modest improvements with complex aggregation metrics (Coverage/Dominance); 'joint 21.3% improvement' lacks clear definition
Reproducibility concerns: code withheld, multiple routing strategies without guidance, implementation details incomplete; Section 6.4 mentions intermediate alignment checkpoints but doesn't explore

strengths: Addresses important problem: clearly demonstrates diversity-quality trade-off with practical implications for open-ended generation tasks
Simple and practical approach: inference-time only, requires no fine-tuning or specialized prompting, deployable with existing models
Exceptionally comprehensive evaluation: 3 datasets, 11×2 metric spaces, novel discourse-level diversity metrics for long-form text, human evaluation across datasets, multiple model families
Strong and consistent empirical results: 21.3% joint improvement in diversity-quality trade-off, 40.5% semantic dominance, consistent across datasets and metrics
Principled routing strategy design: well-organized design space (logit-based and content-based strategies) with clear motivation for each approach
Thoughtful evaluation metrics: Coverage and Dominance metrics from multi-objective optimization elegantly capture complementary aspects (controllability vs. optimality)

Valuable insights: demonstrates importance of semantic vs. lexical metrics, analyzes why heuristic routing outperforms learned routing, identifies inherent failure modes, compares base-aligned vs. aligned-aligned collaboration
Excellent presentation: clear motivation, effective figures, logical flow, good intuition-building
Strong reproducibility efforts: detailed methodology, implementation details in appendices, commitment to release code and data
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core idea of combining base and aligned models is relatively straightforward; hand-crafted heuristic routing rather than learned approaches; heavily inspired by prior work (NUDGING)

Missing efficiency analysis: claims efficiency due to superficial alignment but provides no runtime measurements, latency comparisons, or throughput analysis; computational cost of running two models unknown; critical for practical deployment but empirically unaddressed

Unresolved technical issue - inherent early stop failure mode (Section 6.2): identified when routing to base model but solution (restart sampling) is ad-hoc and increases cost; frequency and performance impact not quantified; raises concerns about fundamental collaborative decoding issues

Limited theoretical understanding: insufficient analysis of why base-aligned collaboration works; superficial alignment hypothesis borrowed but not deeply explored; no characterization of what makes routing strategies effective

Lack of practical deployment guidance: unclear which router to use for which tasks; no sensitivity analysis for routing threshold γ; task-aware router selection mentioned as future work but essential for practitioners

Limited human evaluation: only 20 prompts per dataset, moderate inter-rater agreement on diversity (Fleiss' κ=0.268), all annotators have LLM expertise, no statistical significance testing for human results

Narrow experimental scope: only small models tested (8B, 7B) with unclear scaling properties; only base/aligned pairs from same model family—generalization to other pairs and model families unexplored; only two model families (Llama-3, OLMo2)

Modest optimization margins: best router shows only modest improvements over other strategies (Table 3), suggesting limited room for optimization; improvements on composite metrics (21.3%) while solid, are not exceptional
Missing sensitivity analysis: no analysis of performance variation with routing threshold γ; limited ablation studies on key design choices; no quantification of early-stopping frequency or impact

Incomplete baseline comparisons: limited comparison with other recent diversity-promoting methods; ensemble baselines appear weak; only one collaborative baseline (NUDGING); training-time diversity methods under-explored
